traces.rule: a capture needs at least one jump; must capture only if a piece can jump
traces.sentence: The side to move must capture if any of its pieces can; then it plays the complete capture that takes the most pieces, choosing among equals the one whose piece starts on the lowest-numbered square, then the one whose list of landing squares, read in order, is lower at the first place the lists differ, whatever its last landing.
traces.note: gen_captures records a zero-jump 'capture' for every piece that cannot jump (rec with no moves and captured_count 0), so every position has a capture and the side plays a null move by its lowest-numbered piece instead of stepping or losing; e.g. case 13 (opening position, 40 plies) returns the board unchanged with 40 moves played, case 9 returns 5 played and result 0 instead of white having no move (result 2). Dropping only zero-jump results makes all 13 cases and the visible example pass (rerun with python3 this session). Reading 'a sequence of jumps' as including the empty one would make the step sentence ('If it cannot capture it makes the step...') never apply, and the visible example fails under it, so not a defensible reading.

traces.rule: match each valid pattern against the strings
traces.sentence: For each string, return whether the whole string matches the pattern, and the length of the longest start of it (from no letters up to all of them) that matches, or -1 if none does.
traces.note: Every valid pattern crashes with TypeError: unhashable type: 'list' because the matcher memoises on (node, pos) and the parse tree nodes hold lists; only invalid patterns (which return before matching) pass. Recorded traceback on every listed case; the visible example crashes the same way.

traces.rule: a white man is crowned on row 0
traces.sentence: except that a man that lands on the far row (row 0 for white, row 7 for black) is crowned king and its capture ends there.
traces.note: The answer crowns a white man when its landing square is below 8 (rows 0 and 1) instead of below 4 (row 0), in both captures and steps. In case 13 at ply 23 white jumps 14 over 9 to 5 (row 1) and the answer makes it a king and ends play differently; changing 'l < 8' and 't < 8' to '< 4' makes all 19 cases pass (rerun this session).

traces.rule: postfix operators '*', '+', '?' on an item
traces.sentence: A postfix operator applies to its item's atom together with any operators already after it, so ab* repeats only the b and (a*)? is a*?: '*' matches zero or more repeats, '+' one or more, '?' zero or one.
traces.note: Any item with a postfix operator crashes: closure/plus/optional call m(s, q) but the base matcher takes one argument (TypeError: base() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given; case 12 instead hits unhashable list). Fixing the call alone makes 9, 12, 14, 16, 20, 21, 25 pass; 13, 15, 17, 18 also contain a group and would still fail on the group bug traced separately (they pass once both are fixed).

traces.rule: a parenthesised alternation is an atom
traces.sentence: an atom is a letter, '.', or '(' alternation ')'.
traces.note: parse_atom wraps a group as ('alt', ('alt', seqs)), which match_node cannot walk, so a group never matches anything. Case 23 '()b*?' returns all false/-1 instead of all true; returning the inner alternation fixes it (and, with the operator fix, every failing case and the visible example pass; rerun this session).

traces.rule: the run must finish within the step budget at the stated maximum size
traces.sentence: Each run may take up to 1,000,000 steps.
traces.note: Case 25 is the largest size the task allows (20-token pattern (a*)x10, 8 strings of 12 letters) and traps fuel-exhausted. Run this session on the same pattern with one 12-letter string, the answer gives the right result but costs vm_cost 366,324 steps, so eight strings need about 2.9 million; a performance mistake against the step budget and the bounds ('pattern has at most 20 tokens... lens has 1 to 8 values, each 0 to 12'), not a reading.

traces.rule: up to 12 players
traces.sentence: ratings has 2 to 12 values, each 1,000 to 3,000; rounds is 1 to 7 and below the number of players; results has rounds times (the number of players divided by 2, rounded down) values, each 0 to 2.
traces.note: All state lives in one 240-int sequence with Buchholz at 232+p (also read by the ranking comparator every round), which is out of range for player 8 and up; case 16 has 12 players and traps primitive-fault. Run this session with the sequence enlarged to 260, it returns the expected result exactly.

traces.rule: up to 12 players
traces.sentence: ratings has 2 to 12 values, each 1,000 to 3,000; rounds is 1 to 7 and below the number of players; results has rounds times (the number of players divided by 2, rounded down) values, each 0 to 2.
traces.note: All state lives in one 300-int sequence with the paired-this-round flags at 290+p, out of range for player 10 and up; case 16 has 12 players and traps primitive-fault. Run this session with the sequence enlarged to 320, it returns the expected result exactly.

traces.rule: report one result per string
traces.sentence: For each string, return whether the whole string matches the pattern, and the length of the longest start of it (from no letters up to all of them) that matches, or -1 if none does.
traces.note: Memory-layout overlap: the number of strings is stored in slot 25 but each string's letters are copied to slots 24 onward, so a string of 2 or more letters overwrites the count and the loop stops early, giving full/longest lists of length 0 or 1 (count is sometimes right by chance; invalid case 24 fails the same way). Moving the count to slot 99 makes all 16 cases and the visible example pass (firth_run.py this session).

traces.rule: undoing a push moves the box back
traces.sentence: An undo takes back the latest move in the history and removes it from the history: the worker moves back the way it came, and if that move was a push, its box moves back too.
traces.note: On undoing a push the answer sets the box to player + d, which is where the box already is, so the box never moves back (case 3: two pushes right then undos leave the box at 9 instead of 8). Setting it to the worker's cell instead fixes both cases and the visible example (rerun this session).

traces.rule: a jumping piece leaves the square it jumped from
traces.sentence: A jump moves a piece over a diagonally next square holding a piece of the other side, in a direction it may move, to the empty square just beyond; the piece jumped over is taken off the board at once, and the square the capturing piece started from counts as empty during the capture, so it may land there.
traces.note: During a multi-jump the answer writes the piece on each landing square but never clears the square it jumps from (other than the start), so the final board keeps copies of the piece on every intermediate landing (case 3: white ends on 13 with a ghost on 22). Clearing the current square before recursing makes all six cases and the visible example pass (rerun this session).
